basics.name: Guanyu Mi
basics.about:
I am an AI Researcher and MS ECE candidate at UC Davis, specializing in Agentic Systems and Language Model reasoning limits.

Currently, as a Research Assistant at the Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) Lab, my research extends the Search-R1 framework to explore multi-hop search and test-time compute scaling (pass@k) for agentic small language models (SLMs). My daily work involves synthesizing high-quality golden trajectories, architecting multi-turn RL frameworks with veRL, and pushing the boundaries of AI reasoning capabilities on complex benchmarks like MuSiQue.

Beyond algorithmic research, I have a strong foundation in building end-to-end systems. Having previously developed real-time C++ firmware and custom data acquisition pipelines (PyQt/BLE) for sensor devices, I am adept at bridging hardware with software and processing low-latency data streams. 

I am actively seeking AI/Machine Learning Engineering roles where I can leverage my expertise in LLM reasoning, agentic ai, and reinforcement learning.

education.institution: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

experience.facility: Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) Lab, Advised by Prof. Yubei Chen
description: Extending the Search‑R1 research on multi‑hop search to explore reasoning limits for an agentic 4B‑parameter LLM on the MuSiQue benchmark.
Built a data synthesis pipeline using the Gemini API to construct golden trajectories; achieved a 2.7x exact match increase (from 0.090 to 0.243) after optimizing tool‑calling and cold‑start SFT.
Conducting ablation studies on pass@k scaling laws to evaluate reasoning performance as generation attempts scale, establishing upper bounds for search capabilities.
Architecting a multi‑turn reinforcement learning framework based on veRL to further optimize reasoning and retrieval policies.

Architected an end‑to‑end data acquisition system featuring low‑power BLE transmission and a custom PyQt application for real‑time multi‑channel sensor parsing, synchronization, and visualization.

projects.name: Adaptive Mock Interview Plugin
description: Developing a Modular Monolith extension for the open‑source Resume‑Matcher system, embedding custom FastAPI routers to deliver a native, interactive mock‑interview experience.
Engineering a dynamic GenAI pipeline using LangChain and structured outputs to generate context‑aware technical questions based on resume‑JD gap analysis, effectively eliminating LLM hallucinations.

Designing an SQLite data pipeline to track user performance metrics, which feeds into a scikit‑learn predictive model being trained to dynamically adjust question difficulty based on individual learning curves.

projects.name: Real-Time Sensor Data Acquisition System
description: Reproduced the key experiments from the Logic‑RL paper by assembling a fine‑tuning workflow using existing tools such as Unsloth, LoRA, TRL, and vLLM, enabling DeepSeek‑R1‑style reasoning training on a single 16GB V100 GPU.

Performed systematic hyperparameter tuning through TensorBoard‑based analysis, adjusting KL‑penalty weights and reward configurations to identify a locally optimal setup under limited computing resources.
